hotContext.criticalNews: Fremont S/X line teardown complete and leadership projecting confidence, but full-scale Optimus production has still not been confirmed as started as the late-July/August window opens. Shareholders are demanding ramp status, factory deployment plans, and 2027 external sales numbers ahead of the July 22 earnings call. Competitors (Agility Digit, Xpeng Iron) are commercializing or targeting commercial timelines while Tesla remains pre-revenue on Optimus.

recentKeyChanges.title: Shareholders put Optimus production ramp under Q2 earnings spotlight — no commercial path yet
recentKeyChanges.description: Ahead of Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, shareholder questions submitted via Say Technologies put Optimus Gen 3 at the center of investor scrutiny. The top question (by share-weighted votes) asks for the 'current status of Optimus Gen 3 production ramp,' tasks the robot will perform by end of 2027, and 'initial deployment in factories, and external sales timeline/volume for 2027.' Benzinga and Electrek both report Optimus among the most-upvoted topics. Electrek notes the soft production-status questions were whale-boosted (~4.8M shares each) while harder accountability questions on missed short-term goals dominate the rest of the top 20. Reality check: full-scale Fremont production is still only targeted for late July/August 2026; Musk already warned output will be 'extremely slow'; all 2026 units remain for internal testing with no commercial customers or pricing; and Tesla's $1T Musk pay package still hinges on 1M Optimus units among other milestones. Investors are asking for a production and sales roadmap Tesla has not delivered.

positive_signals: Optimus Gen 3 remains top investor focus — capital markets still price robotics as core Tesla thesis
Fremont S/X line already decommissioned and first production line reported set up (prior weeks)
Shareholders explicitly asking about factory deployment and 2027 external sales (implies expectation of near-term ramp)
negative_signals: No verified full-scale production start yet despite late-July/August target now days away
Investors must ask for production ramp status, factory deployment, and 2027 external sales timeline — none publicly confirmed
All 2026 Optimus units still internal-only; no commercial revenue path disclosed
Musk already pre-announced 'extremely slow' initial output and 'literally impossible to predict' rates (10,000 unique parts)
Electrek: retail tone shifted from vision questions to why short-term goals keep being missed
Softball Optimus questions appear share-weighted to the top while accountability questions dominate true retail interest
1M Optimus units remain a Musk pay-package milestone with zero commercial units delivered

key_metrics.actual: Pre-ramp / limited Gen 3; full-scale Fremont start still targeted late July–August 2026; no commercial sales
key_metrics.target: Investor-requested: factory deployment + 2027 external sales volume; pay package implies 1M Optimus units
key_metrics.trajectory: Facility conversion done; production start imminent but management already lowering ramp expectations; commercialization still 2027+

recentKeyChanges.title: Agility Robotics opens Fremont training hub as Digit already earns revenue — Optimus still pre-commercial
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 17, 2026, TechCrunch reported Agility Robotics is opening a 60,000-square-foot humanoid training facility in Fremont, California — just up the highway from Tesla's Fremont plant where Optimus full-scale production is expected this summer. Agility's Digit robot is already generating revenue moving totes/bins for Amazon, GXO, Schaeffler, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, with ~$300M in contract orders. Agility is pursuing a reverse-merger expected to make it the first pure-play public humanoid company later in 2026. CEO Peggy Johnson emphasized Agility has already commercialized: safety/regulatory compliance, IT integration, and warehouse management system plug-in. Outside estimates put Digit deployments in the dozens (not thousands), but the competitive contrast is stark: Digit does paid warehouse work today while Tesla's deployed Optimus units still do no useful commercial work, and 2026 Optimus output is internal-only. Combined with Xpeng targeting 2027 global launch of its Iron robot (SCMP, July 16), the humanoid race is no longer Tesla-only narrative.

positive_signals: Competitor presence near Fremont validates humanoid market seriousness and local robotics cluster
Tesla still has unmatched capital and manufacturing scale ambition (1M/yr Fremont, 10M/yr Giga Texas targets)
negative_signals: Agility Digit already in paid multi-customer warehouse deployments; Optimus has zero commercial customers
Agility claims ~$300M contract orders; Tesla has no Optimus order book or pricing for external sales
Agility training facility opens in Tesla's backyard as Optimus full-scale production has not yet started
Agility advancing toward public markets as pure-play humanoid; Tesla Optimus still pre-revenue robotics story
Xpeng separately eyes 2027 global Iron robot launch — Chinese competitors also racing Tesla
Musk's own framing: Optimus useful 'outside of Tesla sometime next year' (2027) — admits no external usefulness yet

key_metrics.actual: Optimus: pre-commercial, internal testing only; Agility Digit: multi-customer revenue, ~$300M orders
key_metrics.target: Tesla: public Optimus sales end-2027 at $20–30k (Musk WEF claim); useful outside Tesla 'sometime next year'
key_metrics.trajectory: Competitors commercializing first at small scale while Tesla bets on delayed high-volume manufacturing

recentKeyChanges.title: Elluswamy hails Optimus after S/X line teardown — confidence messaging, zero new production data
recentKeyChanges.description: On or around July 13, 2026, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy responded to Tesla Manufacturing's Model S/X decommissioning video (already covered July 10) with: 'Big shoes to fill, but I'm confident Optimus will not disappoint!!' Covered by Benzinga, Yahoo Finance, and others. VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy has said the facility could see up to ~40 production lines due to Optimus's complex design. This is leadership morale/PR on a facility conversion already in the tracker — not a production-start confirmation, yield figure, unit count, or capability demo. Full-scale output remains targeted late July/August with Musk's 'extremely slow' caveat intact.

positive_signals: AI lead publicly committing confidence as Fremont converts to Optimus
Prior: first Optimus production line reported set up; S/X teardown complete in 46 days
Moravy comment implies multi-line ambition (~40 lines) for complex robot manufacturing
negative_signals: No new unit counts, yield, takt time, or production-start confirmation
Statement is pure confidence PR on already-reported facility teardown
Full-scale production still not running; late July/August target not yet met as of mid-July
Does not address Musk's 'extremely slow' ramp warning or 10,000 unique parts constraint
Does not address commercial capability — robots still not doing useful external work

key_metrics.actual: Facility conversion complete; limited Gen 3; no full-scale rate disclosed
key_metrics.target: Full-scale Optimus production late July/August 2026 at Fremont
key_metrics.trajectory: On facility timeline; production rate and usefulness still unproven
